result:
I repaired F-DG5-102 and F-DG5-145 (one defect: the ADR-0002 module-boundary test timing out under review load). The walk is now about 27% cheaper and the test has its own 150 s budget. Every check in the assignment exits 0. The changes are uncommitted for you to integrate.

**Cause.** For rule 4 (fail on a syntax error), each of the 448 module files went through `ts.transpileModule`. That re-parses the file and then also emits JavaScript, which was always thrown away; the emit was about a third of the walk. The walk itself was already done once per module, and the second parse has to stay: rule 4 must parse the file as the compiler does (for example, a type annotation in a `.js` file is an error), which differs on purpose from the parse the other rules use.

**Fix** (only `apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts` and `apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts` changed):
- **Cheaper walk** (`architecture.testkit.ts:551-562`): `syntaxErrors` still calls `ts.transpileModule` with the same input and options, but an `EMPTY_EMIT` transformer hands the printer an empty tree. TypeScript collects the diagnostics before the emit starts, and this kind of emit adds none of its own, so no diagnostic changes. A faster option (0.9–1.3 s) re-implemented TypeScript internals and could drift on an upgrade, so I didn't use it.
- **Own budget** (`architecture.test.ts:64-65`, `:201-215`): `FULL_MODULE_WALK_TIMEOUT_MS = 150_000`, more than 2x the 67 s loaded worst case. The comment cites F-DG2-143, F-DG5-102/145 and D-174 with the measurements; the assertion is unchanged.
- **Shared 30 s budget unchanged:** the five module-owned tests that use it take 0.3–1.9 s alone, under a third of 30 s.
- **New guard test** (`architecture.test.ts:1078-1134`): it checks that rule 4 reports exactly what a full `transpileModule` reports, across all 8 extensions.
  - Two deliberate breakages were caught (exit 1).
  - A third (target ES2015) was not caught. That change doesn't alter any syntax diagnostic this corpus produces, so it's equivalent here; I disclosed it.
  - A wider comparison over 10,752 cases (448 files in broken and unbroken variants) found 0 differences on both Node versions.
- **Controls unchanged:** all 139 existing tests, including every negative and positive control, pass without edits.

**The test alone** (three runs each):

| Node | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 24 | 7723 / 8378 / 8096 ms | 5726 / 6007 / 6005 ms |
| 22 | 10292 / 8895 / 8891 ms | 5991 / 7099 / 7098 ms |

**Whole `unit-node` project:** 115.3 s before, 105–118 s after. That's unchanged in practice, because other suites and machine load dominate it. Inside those runs, this test fell from 13.6 s to 7.9–10.9 s.

**Checks** (all exit 0):
- `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG4`, at the start and at the end.
- `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, the prettier check (re-run after writing the handback) and `pnpm openapi:lint` (846 operations).
- `unit-node` on Node 24 and Node 22, each with the locale unset and with `C.UTF-8`: 144 files and 2341/2341 tests each (one test more than before, the new guard).
- The one stderr block (`branding.test.ts`) appears both before and after, and is unrelated.
- **Not run (D-164):** the repo-wide `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration` and the full e2e suite. They're for your merged-tree verification.

**For the handback contract:** there are no migrations, API endpoints, contract, schema or dependency changes, and no user-facing text was touched. No ADR or data-dictionary statement is made untrue; I list one optional completeness note for T-DG5-ARCH-R6. The `demo.test.ts` teardown budget in D-174 belongs to T-DG5-BE-Y1, as its assignment says.

The loaded behaviour can only be confirmed by the round-4 reviewers.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/`:
- T-DG5-BE-Y2-backend-workflow-engineer.md
- T-DG5-BE-Y2-evidence/
